I've been farming this 14 mu for 25 years now, ever since I was 20. My old man taught me the basics, and over the years I picked up a few things from the county training sessions and the input dealer in town. I farm the wheat-maize double crop system like everyone else in Quzhou County — winter wheat from October to June, then summer maize from June to October on the same land.

For the wheat, last year I used the improved variety that my neighbor Lao Zhang switched to a few years back. His yields went up from about 450 jin per mu to over 500 jin, so I started buying the same seed. I plant about 25 jin of seed per mu. For fertilizer, I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting time — that's 50 kg of the 15-15-15 stuff from the dealer, so that's 7.5 kg each of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. Then in the spring when the wheat turns green, I top dress with another 20 kg of urea per mu, which gives about 9 kg more nitrogen. I also throw in a little extra potassium sometimes because the dealer says our soil here is a bit low on it, so I add 5 kg of potassium chloride per mu. Total that's about 16.5 kg nitrogen, 7.5 kg phosphorus, and 12 kg potassium per mu. Better to put a bit more than risk a bad harvest — a failed crop means I can't pay for my kid's school expenses.

I irrigate the wheat three times: once before winter to help it survive the cold, once at jointing when it starts growing fast in spring, and once at grain filling. If it's a dry spring I might add one more, but three usually does it. For pesticides, I spray twice — once for weeds right after planting, and once for aphids or rust around heading time. Sometimes three if the bugs are bad.

For the maize, I buy hybrid seed — Zhengdan 958 or something similar, whatever the dealer has that my neighbors are buying. I plant about 3 kg of seed per mu. I put down 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting — the 16-16-16 kind — that's about 6.4 kg each of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. Then at the big trumpet leaf stage, I top dress with 25 kg of urea per mu, which is about 11.5 kg nitrogen. So total around 18 kg nitrogen, 6.4 kg phosphorus, and 6.4 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice — once after sowing if it hasn't rained, and once at tasseling/flowering when the ears are forming. Three times if it's a drought year like two years ago. Pesticide is twice: once for weeds, once for corn borers or armyworms.

For tillage, I plough the field before planting wheat in October — turn the soil over deep to bury the maize stubble. After I harvest the wheat in June, I don't have much time before maize sowing, so I just do rotary tillage to chop up the wheat stubble and level the field. That's what everyone around here does.

I expect my wheat to yield about 520 kg per mu and the maize about 630 kg per mu if the weather cooperates. Last year I got about 500 kg wheat and 620 kg maize, so I'm hoping for a little better this year. I have to watch my budget though — with six people in the house, every yuan counts. I spend about 400 yuan per mu on fertilizer and pesticide for the whole year, and I need to save some money for harvesting labor since my back isn't what it used to be.
